newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TO FUND STATE BROADCASTER TO MARCH.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TO FUND STATE BROADCASTER TO MARCH.

text.p: The South African government has agreed to pick up the tab for public service broadcasting by the state-owned radio and television corporation for the six months to March, Minister Jay Naidoo said on Tuesday.

Naidoo, Minister of Posts, Telecommunications and Broadcasting, said the subsidy would fund the state-owned South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) through the switch from a financial year ending in September to one matching the fiscal year ending in March.

"We are in the process of finalising the details of this funding through a task team comprising the Department of Communications, the Department of State Expenditure and the SABC's Finance division," he said.
Naidoo said a working figure was on the table, but declined to name it.

The SABC asked the government last year for a 190 million rand subsidy to cover its new public broadcasting obligations. The amount was not granted and the SABC posted a loss of 60 million rand in the financial year to September.

Government sources said the corporation was likely to ask for more than 100 million rand to cover its public service obligations in the half year to March, when Finance Minister Trevor Manuel will, for the first time in more than 30 years, make a budget allocation to the state-owned broadcaster.
The obligations of the SABC as a public service broadcaster have still to be spelled out in legislation due to go to parliament this year.
Naidoo told Reuters the draft National Public Broadcasting Bill and the Public Broadcasting Services Bill had been withdrawn and would be consolidated into a single proposal.
He said the new bill would establish a target timetable for the transformation of the SABC into a public broadcasting service for all 11 language groups.
